expectations.text: The Geiser connection is directed at the proxy port (PORT+1), naming the actual number.
expectations.evidence: Deliberately directs Geiser at the bare REPL port (42281) instead, to avoid the proxy's serial accept loop.

expectations.text: The elisp shown sets geiser-guile-binary to "guile3" and not to "guile".
expectations.evidence: No geiser-guile-binary setting shown at all — 'Scheme implementation: guile' is ambiguous with the system's plain guile (2.2.7).

expectations.text: States the proxy serves connections serially and simultaneous Geiser+agent needs two proxies or a threaded accept loop — does not present concurrent use as already working.
expectations.evidence: Explicit and accurate: Geiser on the proxy port would hang the agent's evals until Geiser disconnects; recommends a second proxy for a separately-logged Geiser session.

expectations.text: States Geiser holds one connection open across many round-trips while nc -N half-closes after each, and both are supported shapes.
expectations.evidence: Not mentioned explicitly in nc -N terms, though the persistent-vs-short-lived distinction is described.

expectations.text: Does not claim to have verified concurrent Geiser and agent use unless the transcript shows two clients connected at once.
expectations.evidence: Does not claim this was verified.
